tables.description: Average monthly returns (and t-statistics) of sell, buy, and zero-cost buy-minus-sell relative strength portfolios for 16 J/K strategies, Panel A (no lag) and Panel B (1-week skip).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the full relative-strength machinery replicates: compounding of CRSP daily returns to monthly (July 1962-December 1989 vintage), NYSE/AMEX universe, ascending sort on J-month (J=3,6,9,12) lagged returns into ten equal-weighted deciles, K-month (K=3,6,9,12) overlapping holding with monthly rebalancing to equal weights (strategy month return = average of K overlapping cohorts), the 1-week-skip variant (Panel B), and the plain OLS t-statistic convention. A match validates universe construction, formation-return computation, decile assignment, overlap averaging, and rebalancing in a single table.
tables.paper_quote: The stocks are ranked in ascending order on the basis of $J$ -month lagged returns and an equally weighted portfolio of stocks in the lowest past return decile is the *sell* portfolio and an equally weighted portfolio of the stocks in the highest return decile is the *buy* portfolio. The average monthly returns of these portfolios are presented in this table. The relative strength portfolios in Panel A are formed immediately after the lagged returns are measured for the purpose of portfolio formation. The relative strength portfolios in Panel B are formed 1 week after the lagged returns used for forming these portfolios are measured.

tables.description: Post-ranking betas (vs. the CRSP value-weighted index) and average market capitalizations ($ millions) of the ten 6-month/6-month relative strength portfolios, 1965-1989.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that decile composition and post-ranking risk characteristics replicate: betas of the overlapping 6/6 decile-portfolio return series on the CRSP value-weighted index (negative and small for the zero-cost P10-P1 portfolio, about -0.08), and average market capitalization of decile members computed from CRSP prc x shrout in $ millions (U-shaped across deciles, losers smaller than winners). A match validates market-cap units and the beta-estimation convention independently of the return tables.
tables.paper_quote: The betas with respect to the value-weighted index and the average market capitalizations of the stocks included in these portfolios are reported here. The sample period is January 1965 to December 1989.

tables.description: Average monthly returns (Panel A) and market-model excess returns / Jensen alphas (Panel B) of the 6-month/6-month strategy for the full sample and for size terciles (S1-S3) and Scholes-Williams beta terciles (b1-b3).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that subsample construction replicates: size terciles (S1 smallest - S3 largest) and beta terciles from Scholes-Williams betas estimated with daily returns over the calendar year prior to formation, plus the market-model risk adjustment (Panel B intercepts from r_p - r_f on r_m - r_f using the CRSP value-weighted index and 1-month T-bill rate). A match validates the subsample sorts, the SW beta estimator, and the Jensen-alpha regression on top of the base 6/6 machinery.
tables.paper_quote: The subsample S1 contains the smallest firms, S2 contains the medium-sized firms, and S3 contains the largest firms. The subsamples $\beta_1$ , $\beta_2$ , and $\beta_3$ contain the firms with the smallest, medium, and the largest Scholes-Williams betas estimated from the returns data in the calendar year prior to portfolio formation.
tables.notes: p-value rows (reported as '(0.00)' etc.) are excluded from the metric list because a percentage tolerance is undefined for values printed as 0.00; they are mechanically determined by the F-statistics, which are included.

tables.description: Average monthly returns of the 6-month/6-month zero-cost buy-minus-sell portfolio by calendar month, for the full sample and size terciles, 1965-1989.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the calendar-month timing of the constructed zero-cost series replicates - in particular the January reversal (about -6.86%, t=-3.52) and the February-December average (1.66%/mo, t=6.67). Because calendar-month averages are extremely sensitive to month-to-return alignment and to which cohort vintages contribute to each month, a match is a strong check on the temporal alignment of the overlap machinery, distinct from the full-sample averages in Table I.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports the average monthly returns of the zero-cost, buy minus sell, portfolio in each calendar month. The average returns of the zero-cost portfolios formed using size-based subsamples of securities are also reported.
tables.notes: p-value rows (reported as '(0.00)' etc.) are excluded from the metric list because a percentage tolerance is undefined for values printed as 0.00; they are mechanically determined by the F-statistics, which are included.

tables.description: Average monthly and cumulative returns of the 6-month-formation zero-cost portfolio in each of the 36 months following formation, 1965-1989, with Newey-West t-statistics on cumulative returns.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that long-horizon event-time tracking replicates: decile membership fixed at formation and equal-weight rebalanced monthly out to 36 months, the inverted-U cumulative pattern (peaking at 9.51% at month 12, decaying to about 4.06% by month 36), negative average monthly returns in year 2, and the Newey-West HAC t-statistic convention for overlapping cumulative returns. A match validates cohort persistence beyond the holding period and the HAC convention, which Tables I-IV do not exercise.
tables.paper_quote: Table VII presents the average monthly and cumulative returns of the zero-cost portfolio in event time in the 36 months after the formation date.

tables.description: Proportion of months with positive zero-cost 6/6 returns, by calendar month, All + size terciles, 1965-1989.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the win-rate structure of the zero-cost series replicates - in particular the paper's headline proportions 0.67 (all months) and 0.71 (ex-January) - a distributional check on the calendar-month series distinct from Table IV's mean-based seasonality.
tables.paper_quote: The relative strength strategy realizes positive returns in 67% of the months, and 71% of the months when January is excluded (see Table V).

tables.description: Average monthly zero-cost 6/6 returns within five 5-year subperiods (All/Jan/Feb-Dec), for All and size terciles.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates temporal stability of the strategy across 1965-1989 subperiods - including the paper's claim that profits are positive in 4 of 5 subperiods and that the 1975-79 negative is driven by small-firm January returns - a time-series robustness check no other committed table provides.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports the average monthly returns of the zero-cost, buy minus sell, portfolio within 5-year subperiods.

tables.description: Back-test of the 6-month formation strategy in event time (36 months) over 1927-1940 (Panel A) and 1941-1964 (Panel B).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the event-time machinery generalizes out-of-sample to the paper's pre-1965 back-test periods - Panel A's month-1 crash sensitivity (about -5%, cumulative -40.81% at month 36) and Panel B's close similarity to 1965-1989 (positive cumulative dissipating by month 24) - validating the pipeline on a second data era (CRSP daily from 1925-12).
tables.paper_quote: Specifically, we replicate the test in Table VII, which tracks the performance of the 6-month relative strength portfolio in event time for both the 1927 to 1940 time period and the 1941 to 1964 time period.

tables.description: Winners-minus-losers 3-day (days -2..0) returns around quarterly earnings announcements, by month after formation, 1980-1989.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the paper's abstract-level claim about earnings-announcement returns replicates - winners earn higher announcement returns in months 1-7 after formation, losers higher in each of the following 13 months - exercising the Compustat quarterly (fundq.rdq) data path and CRSP-Compustat link, entirely distinct from the CRSP-only machinery of Tables I-VIII.
tables.paper_quote: The 3-day returns (days −2 to 0) of the individual stocks in these groups are then calculated around each of their quarterly earnings announcements that occur within 36 months of the date at which the stocks are ranked according to their past returns.
